name_note: Most genomes GTDB places in this genus carry the NCBI name Ruminococcus, so much of the relevant literature uses Ruminococcus species names rather than Ruminococcoides.

sentences.text: Ruminococcoides is a bacterial genus abundant in the human colon that plays a key role in carbohydrate metabolism and can use a variety of growth substrates.
Ruminococcoides bili, isolated from human faeces, degrades resistant starch strongly using glycoside hydrolases, carbohydrate-binding modules and amylosome-like multienzyme complexes.
In resistant-starch-rich conditions the bacterium strongly upregulates distinctive scaffoldin proteins that organise these starch-degrading complexes.
